articles.title: Mexico City GP: Charles Leclerc dominates first practice from Kimi Antonelli as Ferrari show strong pace
articles.summary: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc put down a statement time in first practice to be more than half a second clear of the field, including Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli; watch every session of the Mexico City GP live on Sky Sports F1, with Friday's second practice at 10pm
articles.body:
Leclerc was 0.659s quicker than Antonelli to underline the expectation that Ferrari will be strong at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez due to their small turbo working well at high altitude.

Lewis Hamilton was fourth after a scruffy soft-tyre lap but will be buoyed by his team-mate's pace as Ferrari look to win only their third race of the season.

It should not majorly impact Antonelli on the weekend where he is likely to become world champion on Sunday as he only needs a top-nine finish to secure the drivers' title.

Ten rookies replaced the usual full-time drivers in first practice as most teams took advantage of the relative simplicity of the circuit and it not being a Sprint weekend to fulfil a regulation that a rookie most run in both cars at least twice in the season - only Ferrari ran both regular drivers in the session.

Mercedes reserve driver and 2023 Formula 2 runner-up Frederik Vesti was the best of the rookies in third, less than one tenth behind Antonelli, and Ayumu Iwasa also impressed in Max Verstappen's Red Bull in fifth, less than one second off the pace on the medium tyres.

Perhaps most notably, Formula 2 driver Colton Herta completed 24 laps in the session which meant he drove for 100km, so has been awarded another super-licence point.

Herta now has 39 super-licence points, so is just one point away from being eligible to become a full-time Formula 1 driver and it is understood senior figures at Cadillac are keen to give him a drive in 2027. Cadillac may give Herta another opportunity in the remaining four rounds to gain another point and secure a super-licence.

Although Valtteri Bottas signed a multi-year contract when he joined the newcomers at the start of this year, his seat is under threat for next year from American Herta.

Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson is the other driver whose future is up in the air, despite an impressive season that sees him ninth in the Drivers' Championship, as Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov could become Formula 2 champion and Red Bull have traditionally promoted their young drivers quickly.

Estonian driver Tsolov made his practice debut in Mexico for Racing Bulls on Friday and was only one tenth behind Arvid Lindblad, overcoming an issue where he stated blood had stopped flowing in his right leg due to his seat compressing while driving.

British teenager Freddie Slater also made his first F1 practice outing for Audi but was limited to just 14 laps due to an issue, and Aston Martin rookie Jak Crawford also stopped on track with a technical issue.

Audi are under investigation for sending Slater out onto the track with a cooling fan on his car and are likely to be handed a big fine.

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar suffered a power-unit problem early in the session but did not complete any serious qualifying simulations.

All the full-time drivers will return in second practice later on Friday at 10pm, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event.

articles.title: Mexico City Grand Prix practice result: Charles Leclerc fastest in Ferrari
articles.summary: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc goes fastest in Friday practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc headed McLaren's Lando Norris in Friday practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, who is poised to clinch his first world title on Sunday, was fourth fastest behind team-mate George Russell.

Only a victory by Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton can theoretically stop Antonelli becoming champion on Sunday. Even then, Antonelli only needs ninth place if Russell wins and 10th if Hamilton does.

Leclerc, who topped both sessions on Friday, was 0.103 seconds quicker than Norris, with Russell just 0.003secs further adrift.

Antonelli was 0.217secs off the pace, and ahead of the Red Bulls of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

Leclerc's team-mate Lewis Hamilton was 11th overall after stopping on track with a technical problem before completing his qualifying simulation runs on the soft tyre.

Behind Hadjar, Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson sandwiched Pierre Gasly's Alpine, while McLaren's Oscar Piastri completed the top 10.

Verstappen and Lawson face a trip to the stewards after a collision in the stadium early in the session.

"I don't think it's called unlucky," said Verstappen. "Maybe not very smart behaviour what he was trying to do there.

"At the end of the day it is not going to change my weekend, but if I were him I would act a little smarter and when you're fighting for your seat it's not very smart behaviour."

Lawson is one of three drivers competing for two seats at Racing Bulls, Red Bull's junior team, next year, alongside current team-mate Arvid Lindblad and Bulgarian Formula 2 front-runner Nikola Tsolov.

Verstappen added: "When he saw me coming, he suddenly started to accelerate. I don't know what was going through his head, that he wanted to drive me off the track in the hairpin.

"That's not very sensible behavior from someone in his position, to pick a fight with me."

The first session was marked by 10 of the 11 teams running 'rookie' drivers in their cars.

One of them was Cadillac's Colton Herta, who the team are considering promoting to a race seat in place of Valtteri Bottas next season.

Initially, the team felt his running in Mexico had given him enough points under the F1 system to earn a 'superlicence', which is required to race in F1.

But further investigation by governing body the FIA revealed the American nine-time Indycar race winner is still one point short and will have to complete one further practice session this year to secure his licence.

The team plan to do that before the end of the season.

articles.title: Oliver Bearman: Haas boss Ayao Komatsu furiously dismisses reports claiming British driver is demanding £5m annual salary
articles.summary: Watch every Mexico City GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 9pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday
articles.body:
Both Bearman and Komatsu have expressed confidence in recent weeks that a deal will be done to extend the 21-year-old's current contract, which expires at the end of the 2026 season.

With Haas having already announced the signing of Bearman's fellow Ferrari junior Rafael Camara to replace Esteban Ocon next season, the lack of confirmation on his own future has led to speculation over what the issues are that are holding up the deal.

Asked on Friday at the Mexico City Grand Prix about claims that Bearman's financial demands are the main sticking point, Komatsu said: "I have no idea where that comes from.

"I've experienced this sometimes this season as well. People say there's no smoke without fire but really some people will invent a story.

"What happened in Miami? Apparently, I had an argument with (Bearman's team-mate) Esteban Ocon. There's just absolutely zero truth in it and even those people claiming that they had some insider information etc, absolute total nonsense.

"This one again I don't know who smoked up this six-million euros number. The first time I saw it on Instagram, or Stu [Morrison, Haas press officer] forwarded it to me, and I was just like, 'oh another great… somebody has come up and stirred up whatever'.

"I have no comments to make because it's just not even close to the truth. Why do we engage in such an absolute nonsense? What's the point of it?

"Those people clearly are not trying to help anything right? It's amazing these days that people don't check the source.

"So, ok I want to get some more clicks, I want to get some more likes, so they copy and paste those stories and keep running with it, then before you know it, like 20 people are running the stories that they think it's a truth. It's absolute nonsense."

While Komatsu refused to reveal the details that are preventing an agreement from being reached, he insisted the team "want to grow together" with Bearman.

"I don't like to go into the details of our contract," Komatsu said. "Ollie is showing amazing potential. He contributed a lot and he's contributing a lot to the team's success.

"We want to grow together, we want to move up the grid as a team, so first and foremost we need a competitive car.

"2027 is not going to be the easy challenge because 2026 we made a mistake, so that's paying the price for 2027 as well.

"Our focus is really to maximise everything under control, so really trying to roll out a competitive 2027 car and then hopefully we'll have Ollie driving as well and then take it from there."

Bearman remains attached to Ferrari having come through the team's junior programme, and has made no secret of his desire to earn a seat with the Italian squad.

However, he insists that while a seat at Ferrari - or one of F1's other established top teams - remains out of reach, he is keen to continue his F1 journey with Haas.

Speaking on Thursday in Mexico, Bearman said. "I think it's very clear. I want to continue with Haas. That's definitely my goal.

"There are a few things in the background that we're working on, but it's been very clear that continuing with Haas will be my target, and we're just finalising a few things on that front."

Asked about the delay, Bearman insisted that a deal would have been finalised by this point if it was up to him.

"It's not really in my hands, I can tell you that," he added.

"If it was up to me, it would have already been announced a long time ago.

"But there are a few bigger-picture things that we're working on."

articles.title: Leclerc repite en cabeza y Alonso entra en lo inédito, a 0,7 seg.
articles.standfirst: El asturiano confirma que puede ser uno de sus mejores fines de semana del año
articles.summary: El asturiano confirma que puede ser uno de sus mejores fines de semana del año
articles.body: Con todas las limitaciones de un motor que sigue siendo precario, Fernando Alonso terminaba 12º en los libres del del GP de México, en uno de sus mejores resultados de 2026, no tanto por el puesto, sino por las diferencias respecto a la cabeza de la tabla. El 0.769 de distancia con Charles Leclerc, el primero del día, es inédito en lo que va de temporada y una posible señal de que puede estar en posiciones similares a Sepang (octavo) este domingo. La solidez del asturiano en los sectores 2 y 3, donde ha sido uno de los mejores de forma constante, hacen pensar que no será otra carrera de trámite para el '14' en México. El situarse a una décima de Piastri, que marcaba el 'top-ten', es otro buen dato para un Alonso que estuvo casi siempre en posiciones privilegio. Una agradable novedad en este curso, tan amargo como poco alentador, por la falta de potencia bajo el acelerador en el AMR26, que ahora da ciertas señales positivas en eficiencia. En una muy buena sesión en lo personal, extrayendo mucho más de lo que hay en el Williams. Carlos Sainz terminaba 17º, a una décima de Colapinto, pero lejos de poder buscar los puntos el domingo. Era lo que esperaba antes de salir a pista en el Hnos Rodríguez, y este final de temporada sigue siendo un test global para intentar mejorar el chasis de Grove para 2027. articles.title: Mexico City GP: Charles Leclerc completes Friday practice double as Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton suffers technical failure
articles.summary: Charles Leclerc tops both Friday practice sessions for Ferrari; Lewis Hamilton suffers technical failure; Max Verstappen collides with Liam Lawson; watch every Mexico City GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 9pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday
articles.body:
Leclerc produced a time of 1:17.827s to finish just over a tenth clear of McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell, with the British pair among 10 drivers who had earlier sat out the opening session to make way for rookie drivers.

Kimi Antonelli, who only needs to finish ninth in Sunday's race to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion, was a tenth down on his team-mate Russell in fourth.

Hamilton had been on course to go fastest as the session approached its midway point before suffering what appeared to be an engine issue in the final sector of his push lap, leaving him 11th.

He completed the lap but was then swiftly told by his engineer to pull over on track, ending his session early and denying him valuable information that his rivals were able to gather with their race simulations.

Max Verstappen, another to have sat out first practice, was three tenths off the pace in fifth, with his team-mate Isack Hadjar slotting in behind him.

Verstappen was involved in a bizarre collision with his former team-mate Liam Lawson in the early stages of the session as the four-time world champion attempted to overtake the Racing Bulls driver.

Lawson defended and retained track position, only for the battle to continue on for several more corners before the pair made contact, leaving debris on the track that caused a red flag to be thrown so it could be cleared.

The pair will not only have to explain themselves to their teams, who are both part of the Red Bull family, but also the stewards as they were called to see them following the session.

Lawson was ninth, two places behind his team-mate Arvid Linbdlad with Alpine's Pierre Gasly splitting the Racing Bulls.

Oscar Piastri endured another disappointing day as he could only manage 10th, finishing more than half a second down on his McLaren team-mate Norris.

Fernando Alonso produced an encouraging result for Aston Martin as he finished within eight tenths of Leclerc in 12th.

articles.title: Horarios F1 libres y clasificación del GP de México: a qué hora es y dónde ver en TV la 'qualy' de Sainz y Alonso
articles.standfirst: Antonelli prefiere conservar para luego atacar
articles.summary: Antonelli prefiere conservar para luego atacar
articles.body: Guerra abierta en Red Bull tras los Libres 2. Max Verstappen y Liam Lawson se acabaron tocando tras un 'pique' durante los primeros compases del segundo entrenamiento. Sin embargo, lo importante se encuentra en los Ferrari, especialmente en Leclerc, quien se llevó el Libre 1 con un tiempo de 1.18.128, en una sesión "invadida" por los 'Rookies'. Siguió el monegasco calcando la buena racha, al igual que hizo ya en Austin la semana pasada, y se llevó de igual forma el Libre 2, con un tiempo de 1.17.827 Mientras, el líder del Mundial, Kimi Antonelli, prefirió no enseñar sus cartas antes de tiempo y guardarse el ataque para cuando es necesario: en 'qually' y carrera. Por ello, el italiano finalizó 2º el Libre 1 a 659 milésimas del monegasco, y 4º el el Libre 2 a 217 milésimas de Leclerc, conservando mucho. Por otro lado, los británicos, George Russell y Lando Norris, aparecieron por sorpresa para colocarse entre las primeras posiciones durante el Libre 2, el único del que formaron parte el viernes, dejando una clasificación muy apretada entre los tres primeros, pues tan sólo 106 milésimas separan al de Ferrari, McLaren y Mercedes. "Son sólo unos Libres 2. No hay que venirse arriba". Esas fueron las palabra de Pedro de la Rosa, embajador de Aston Martin, ante las heroicidades que Fernando Alonso volvió a hacer durante el primer día de prácticas. El asturiano acabó a 1.229 de Leclerc en el primer Entrenamiento Libre, 7º y a 769 milésimas del monegasco durante el Libre 2. Por el contrario, Carlos Sainz parece seguir teniendo demasiados problemas. En ninguna de las dos sesiones pudo ascender de la 15ª posición y, aunque la Q2 es posible, sin lugar a duda el '55' tendrá que luchar con todo lo que tiene. Como es habitual, el Gran Premio de México de Fórmula 1 2026 se podrá ver en directo por televisión a través de DAZN F1 y en Movistar+. También tienes la opción de seguir todo lo que suceda en la carrera en el Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez a través de los directos de MARCA.com y la transmisión de la carrera en Radio MARCA. articles.title: Alonso: "Pensé que aquí podíamos tener una grata sorpresa"
articles.standfirst: El español intuía que su coche podía dar un mejor rendimiento en México
articles.summary: El español intuía que su coche podía dar un mejor rendimiento en México
articles.body: Fernando Alonso reconocía que el AMR26 ha comenzado el GP de México mejor de lo esperado, aunque el bicampeón no descartaba nada de antemano. "Probablemente sí. Llegué con la mente muy abierta, porque México es un lugar único, debido a la altitud y otros factore, así que pensé que quizá nos llevaríamos una grata sorpresa. Por ahora, al menos en mi lado del garaje, el coche funciona bien", deslizaba tras ser 12º en los Libres 2. "Son los desafíos habituales en México: la altitud, la velocidad del turbo, la temperatura, los frenos... cuestiones que rozan el límite. Aparte de eso, no hay grandes preocupaciones para mañana. Este año hay aún menos carga aerodinámica, algo lógico dada la gran altitud", añadía. Fernando confesaba que lo que pasó el viernes era muy similar a lo que recordaba del Hnos Rodríguez. "Sinceramente, no hay una gran diferencia. Todos estábamos preocupados por la falta de carga aerodinámica en comparación con otras carreras, pero, en realidad, el coche se comporta de forma muy similar a como lo ha hecho aquí en años anteriores; así que, diría que no ha supuesto un desafío adicional", matizaba. Lo curioso llegaba, cuando le preguntaban por el motor Hoda. "Hablamos con el señor Orihara el jueves, se mostraba bastante preocupado por el 'turbo lag' (retardo del turbo) y lo complicado que podría resultar aquí. ¿Cuáles son las primeras impresiones al respecto?", se interesaba el periodista de F1 TV. "Esa es una pregunta para él; creo que sigue estando preocupado", contestaba Alonso en tono divertido.
